cross_continuation_convergence.cluster: The non-mutating read fence is not `--ignore-working-copy`
cross_continuation_convergence.what_it_is: Five arms across two continuations independently found that the read mode the Plans name cannot deliver the property the Plans promise. Arm B recommended `--at-op=@ --ignore-working-copy` from jj's own CLI reference; T80 SUPERSEDED that remedy by showing resolve_op_heads performs the ancestor-marker cleanup write BEFORE the @ resolver is reached, so only an explicit operation id is a fence; A24 restated it at the Plans' own v0.44.0 profile and extended it to the whole read command inventory, and added the before/after op-head equality check. The campaign converged on one answer and then corrected itself twice.

candidates.label: JJ restore drill object verification has no stated depth
candidates.proposition: The backup JJ restore-verification receipt must state the verification depth that produced object_closure_result, by reference to the Backup owner's existing integrity_verification_level enum, and object_closure_result: complete must be inadmissible when the depth did not read object content, so an activation-eligible outcome cannot rest on a reachability-only pass.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. Not among continuation 3's four rejected expansions. Worth naming its kinship: continuation 3's own F106 is a correction in the same JJI-008 restore-verification family, found from the field side (a readiness flag admissible under blocked conditions) rather than the depth side.
candidates.distinctness: F081 requires complete native object interpretation and an isolated restore before activation; it does not constrain what depth of checking is allowed to produce the receipt's complete value. This is contradictory/underdetermined content inside an already-present typed receipt, the same shape continuation 3 used to hold F106 distinct from F001.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. Recorded as a candidate with evidence, as the brief requires.

candidates.label: Isolated drill must resolve and rebind in-store location pointers
candidates.proposition: Before any native command runs in the disposable copy, the restore drill must resolve every in-store location pointer (store/git_target, objects/info/alternates, .jj/repo pointer files, linked-workspace gitdir links) and record where each resolved; a pointer resolving outside the isolation boundary is a typed blocker distinct from missing objects and collisions, and is either rebound inside the boundary with the rebinding recorded or blocks the drill, never followed. isolated_verification: true is admissible only when every pointer resolved inside the boundary.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F079 requires alternate and shared stores inside the closure and F081 requires an isolated restore; neither constrains how the restored copy's own pointers resolve at drill time, and no rejected expansion covers it.
candidates.distinctness: F079 requires the capture to include underlying Git/common/alternate/shared stores; F081 requires an isolated restore. Neither constrains how the restored copy's own path pointers are resolved at drill time, which is what makes a same-host drill able to pass by reading the original's objects. The arm itself records that the clean-host condition exists in the BKP-006 lineage packet but survives in current owner text only as a future test surface.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The strongest of the five: it identifies a way to obtain a false complete-recovery badge that the current owner text permits.

candidates.label: Machine-local and ephemeral native store entries have no stated disposition
candidates.proposition: The source closure must record, for the pinned JJ version, an enumerated source-traced classification of machine-local and ephemeral entries inside .jj/repo (native lock files, per-machine store identity files) - captured as bytes but non-authoritative and never restored as active state - never a filename pattern such as '*.lock'; a version change invalidates the list until re-audited, and an unrecognized entry inside the store tree yields partial with a named ref rather than complete.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. Adjacent to F084, which governs restored configuration; this is about machine-local entries inside .jj/repo, which no union finding or rejected expansion addresses.
candidates.distinctness: F084 governs restored configuration, helpers, hooks, filters, includes and credentials. The arm states the gap explicitly: the Plans say what must be sanitized and inactive after restore but say nothing about the machine-local, ephemeral, non-configuration entries inside the store tree.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The negative test (store/extra/lockfile, store/extra/foo.lock, op_heads/locks must not be treated as locks) is the part that makes it more than a restatement of F084.

candidates.label: No blocker class for present-but-unloadable native metadata
candidates.proposition: The JJ drill blocker taxonomy needs one distinct class for a restored copy whose objects and operations are all present but whose native metadata pointers are missing or unmergeable, separate from missing object closure, conflicts, collisions, stale target and operation mismatch; any repair of such state happens only inside the disposable copy and is disclosed in the receipt.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: YES, EFFECTIVELY - and I contested it at the time. Continuation 3 rejected 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor' as 'Refinements/alternatives under existing F082/F086/F056 and their scope boundaries, not additional demonstrated product obligations.' A new blocker class for present-but-unloadable native metadata is a corruption-taxonomy refinement under F082. Recorded, not advanced.
candidates.distinctness: CONTESTED BY THE ADJUDICATOR. Continuation 3's symmetric adjudication already rejected the expansion 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor' with the reason 'Refinements/alternatives under existing F082/F086/F056 and their scope boundaries, not additional demonstrated product obligations.' This candidate is a corruption/blocker taxonomy addition under F082 and falls within that rejected class. Recorded for completeness, flagged as most likely a refinement of F082 rather than a new finding.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union, and additionally flagged as probably inside continuation 3's rejected-expansion class.

candidates.label: gc_fence_outcome held_during_capture does not state what the fence covered
candidates.proposition: gc_fence_outcome: held_during_capture must enumerate the writer paths the fence covered (native JJ process, colocated Git, registered external/automation paths) and assert that no uncovered mutation path into the same store existed for the capture window; if coverage cannot be asserted for a known path the closure is partial with the uncovered path named, and a fence claim with an empty covered-path list is rejected.

Neither addresses a fence held truthfully over one path while another was never covered, which is the case the arm demonstrates externally. Credited separately as baseline support for F004; the contract-level covered-path requirement is the residue recorded here.

Arm C's claim that dojjo 'opts out of the documented mitigation by passing UNIX_EPOCH' is wrong - jj's lib/src/simple_op_store.rs:285-298 removes a file only when mtime <= keep_newer, so UNIX_EPOCH removes nothing. Verified by the adjudicator against the source; deepseek41/J0025 found it. The candidate SURVIVES on its other leg, which is unaffected: the per-instance FsDojoUploadStore io_lock that does not coordinate across concurrent HTTP requests, and the file:// remote path that bypasses the smart-HTTP handler and its lock entirely. candidates.label: No save contract exists for a diff/compare or merge-editor surface
candidates.proposition: A compare/merge surface needs an owner-level save contract: typed per-path actions (write_text with expected-before hash/type, delete, create_symlink{target}, set_mode{executable}, no_change) each carrying a reason category, never a string map; typed exclusions that are not admissible targets without an explicit authorized type transition; a preflight over admission-for-this-compare-identity, parent/type materializability and capacity before the first write; identity binding to repo/worktree plus the expected native revision; application through the FileSafe ledger so failure on file N of M rolls back the whole scope or fences; and third-party tools launched over an isolated tree whose result is imported, never described as atomic when they write the worktree directly.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: PARTIALLY, flagged. It is a merge-editor save surface, which is the subject of the rejected cluster 'Corruption taxonomy, extras detector, clone stage details and arbitrary conflict editor'. Items 1-5 also restate union obligations already credited to the arm.
candidates.distinctness: PARTLY DUPLICATIVE, flagged. Items 1-5 restate obligations already in the union and already credited to this arm (F029 identity and complete matched selections, F031 byte and metadata round-trip, F033 path confinement, F034 partial writes, F037 bounded reads, F056 conflict truth). The genuinely new part is that the Plans name a structured merge editor (UI_Command_Catalog.md:549) and an external merge-tool preference (storage-plan.md:1927) with no save/write contract for either, and item 6's isolated-tree rule for third-party tool execution. Continuation 3 rejected expansions that were 'refinements/alternatives under existing findings and their scope boundaries'; the surface-level gap is the part that escapes that rejection.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union; recorded with the duplication flagged.

candidates.label: cmd.jujutsu.change.split has no expressible non-interactive execution
candidates.proposition: cmd.jujutsu.change.split is canonical, bound to a sole future handler and wired across the catalog, yet the frozen command_target can only name a change_id, and a native `jj split` with no path arguments always launches a diff editor - by default a crossterm terminal UI a Slint workbench cannot host. command_target must gain a closed change_content_selection {selection_kind: whole_change|explicit_paths, repo_relative_paths, interactive_editor: prohibited}, split must require explicit paths, a disabled reason interactive_editor_session_required must exist, and section 3.3 must state that no canonical Jujutsu command may reach an adapter invocation that can start an interactive diff or merge editor.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F028 asks for machine-readable partial-change specifications; this is the prior structural defect that the canonical split command has no expressible non-interactive execution. No rejected expansion covers it.
candidates.distinctness: F028 asks for machine-readable partial-change specifications exposed to agents and scripts, and is credited to this arm. This is the prior structural defect: the owner requires a command whose only expressible native execution is an interactive editor session that the same owner 'never describes, never blocks, and gives no typed result for'. It is a contradiction inside the frozen inventory, not a capability request.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The strongest of this arm's candidates: a canonical command with no admissible execution path.

candidates.label: An unpinned JJ read authors an operation, so capture and drill can mutate what they observe
candidates.proposition: Every JJ read issued by capture, restore verification and inspection must be pinned to an exact operation id and to ignore-working-copy (or RepoLoader::load_at(op), never load_at_head()); divergence must be probed and recorded without being resolved, with every head in operation_head_refs and a distinct divergent closure state; Backup never reconciles; and the verification receipt records the disposable copy's op-head set before and after and asserts equality, with a verification-authored operation a typed failure.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO - and, like the union arm's C4U-01, it lands on the same side as a continuation-3 rejection. Continuation 3 rejected adding a mutating status.refresh branch; this candidate keeps reads non-authoring by pinning them to an exact operation rather than by granting them write authority.
candidates.distinctness: F002 states that nominal reads have effects that must be classified and fenced, and is credited to this arm. This candidate is the specific machine-contract consequence: every PM clause about not manufacturing state names a snapshot, nothing requires a read to be operation-pinned, and all five fixtures carrying operation_head_refs hold exactly one head, so the contract is never exercised against divergence. The arm shows an unpinned read can change op_heads/heads/ even without true divergence, which makes the acceptance check a sharp discriminator.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: allowed_action_ids has no floor, so a blocked repository can admit no recovery action
candidates.proposition: availability_payload.allowed_action_ids carries no conditional of any kind, so an empty array validates for state blocked with disabled_reason_code repository_quarantined. Under Contracts_V0.md:508 recovery actions 'are admitted only when the current blocked episode exposes the corresponding ordered actions', so an empty set means no recovery action is admitted at all. A conditional must require, for the quarantine and staleness reason codes, at least cmd.jujutsu.operation.log and .show, and these must be servable from the operation store alone - without a current working-copy snapshot, a valid writer lease, or a healthy status projection.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F010 and F072 are credited to the arm; neither says an availability payload may admit an empty recovery-action set for a blocked repository. No rejected expansion covers it.
candidates.distinctness: F010 requires native and sidecar state to stay independently observable across partial failure and is credited to this arm. F072 requires one catalog with authoritative eligibility and is also credited. This candidate is the specific unbound field: the arm read all three allOf branches of availability_payload and established that none constrains allowed_action_ids, and that the one shipped availability fixture sets no precedent for the case where the status projection is itself broken.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: bookmark.track and bookmark.untrack are classified as transport mutations requiring a credential lease
candidates.proposition: The schema places cmd.jujutsu.bookmark.track and .untrack in the same conditional as git.clone/fetch/push, narrowing credential_lease_ref to a non-null ref and pinning command_class to transport_mutation, while the frozen fixture sets permission.scope to local_mutation - internally inconsistent. Native untrack and track are purely local view transactions with no remote call and no credential use. Both commands must move to command_class local_mutation with credential_lease_ref null, keeping the writer lease, FileSafe decision, permission snapshot, expected-revision fence and currentness.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F038 concerns credential architecture and F109 transport credential evidence; neither says a purely local command is misclassified as a transport mutation.
candidates.distinctness: Not in the union. F038 concerns credential architecture and custody and F109 concerns transport credential evidence fields; neither says a purely local command is misclassified as transport. The arm shows the user-visible consequence: without a credential lease a user cannot form a schema-valid untrack request at all, and the availability model would surface credential_lease_missing for an operation that never touches a network - against the product's own promise that a person can keep local history without an online service.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. The most concretely falsifiable of the four: an internal inconsistency between a schema branch and its own shipped fixture.

candidates.label: A divergent change has no representable state anywhere in the corpus
candidates.proposition: A divergent change - multiple visible commits sharing one change ID - is a first-class, user-visible jj state arising from ordinary multi-actor use, and the word appears nowhere in any source-control, Jujutsu or GUI context in the Plans. node_state, the GUI graph_states prefix list and the JJ error/disabled-reason enums are all closed without it. Add divergent to node_state and graph_states, add a change_divergent_ambiguous_target reason code, and reject before effect any command whose change target resolves to more than one visible commit unless the request carries the exact commit_id.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F022 is the union's convergence capability and F006 the identity separation, both distinct from the representability gap this names.
candidates.distinctness: F006 requires change and commit identity to stay separate and is credited to this arm; F022 asks for explicit convergence of divergent commits and is recorded as a partial. This candidate is neither: it is that the state cannot be named, shown or refused at all, established by reading the closed enums that would have had to contain it rather than by literal search.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union.

candidates.label: JJI-008 states the ends of closure completeness but names no decision procedure
candidates.proposition: A JJ backup or restore path must transfer and persist dependency objects before publishing any referring head, op-head or bookmark pointer; expand and verify the full operation-to-view-to-commit-to-tree closure for the retained set including non-current, abandoned and rebased objects before reporting complete; reject missing parent files, malformed IDs, self-parents and parent cycles as distinct closure blockers rather than silent skips; materialize restores in dependency-safe order with heads and activation markers last; and activate only after the existing isolated-disposable verification succeeds.
candidates.continuation3_already_rejected: NO. F079 requires the closure contents, barrier and fence; this names the missing decision procedure. Not a rejected expansion.
candidates.distinctness: F079 requires the closure contents and the barrier and fence, and is credited to this arm. This candidate is the missing mechanism: the arm establishes that the Plans 'require the ends ... but name no mechanism - no objects-before-heads publication rule, no operation-to-view-to-commit-to-tree parent-closure expansion with length and missing-file validation, no topological apply order, no missing or cyclic-parent negative cases wired into adapter tests'. claude-hicap reached the same gap independently (its J0027 Gap 1), which strengthens it.
candidates.adjudicator_note: Not added to the union. Independently found by two arms.

candidates.proposition: The closure manifest must record backend-resolved store paths and the environment and inputs that resolve them, including the relevant GIT_* variables or their documented absence and which pointer files were followed; discovery must follow gitfile, commondir and objects/info/alternates chains honouring their distinct bases (alternates relative to the object database, commondir relative to the Git directory) and record each hop's base and target, with unfollowable or out-of-boundary hops surfacing as missing dependencies; and HEAD, index and working-copy material must be captured per workspace while shared commondir content is captured once, with administrative back-pointers rewritten to the disposable boundary.

candidates.label: A 32nd canonical command, cmd.jujutsu.bookmark.forget
candidates.assertion: Add cmd.jujutsu.bookmark.forget so a user whose intent is 'stop tracking this locally, leave the remote alone' has a covered route. At v0.44.0 forget is the ONLY native way to drop a local bookmark without queueing a remote deletion, and native delete's own help text points users at it. Both jobs raise it independently and both recommend NOT exposing --include-remotes in a first cut, because the next fetch recreates the remote bookmark if it still exists upstream - an action that visibly undoes itself.
